facility_roles.quote: Production of the muon beam begins with the extraction of a bunch of 24 GeV/c protons from the AGS.

intervals.label: data taking (runs R97 to R01)
intervals.note: Annual 3-4 month runs 1997-2001 at the AGS (24 GeV/c protons from the AGS produce the muon beam).
intervals.quote: obtained in typically 3-4 month annual runs through 2001. In this paper, we indicate the running periods by the labels R97 - R01.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: End of data taking is taken as the last run label (R01); the storage ring was moved to Fermilab in 2013 for the successor experiment.
intervals.quote: Many people have made important contributions towards the success of E821 over the past twenty years when this experiment was proposed, built and completed.

name: E821 (BNL muon g-2)
notes: Lineage: experiment:muon-g-2 (Fermilab E989) is the successor (it reuses this ring); that edge lives on the existing muon-g-2 record, which this stream does not own (listed for the integrator).

physics_goals.quote: We present the final report from a series of precision measurements of the muon anomalous magnetic moment, a_mu = (g-2)/2.
physics_goals.value: Measure the muon anomalous magnetic moment a_mu = (g-2)/2 with precision measurements using positive and negative muons

summary.plain: The Brookhaven experiment that stored muons in a large magnetic ring and measured how fast their spin turns, giving the muon’s anomalous magnetic moment to 0.54 parts per million, fourteen times better than before. Its ring was later moved to Fermilab.
summary.technical: BNL E821 at the AGS: muon storage ring measuring a_mu = (g-2)/2 with nearly equal samples of positive and negative muons, 1997-2001; final a_mu(Expt) = 11 659 208.0(5.4)(3.3) x 10^-10 (0.54 ppm). The same ring was relocated to Fermilab in 2013 for E989.
